query: Which material can be used for enhanced catalytic activity and durability toward HER and HOR, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Transition metal dichalcogenides, such as molybdenum disulfide (MoS2), can be used for enhanced catalytic activity and durability toward the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and hydrogen oxidation reaction (HOR).
generation.conditions: Acidic or alkaline electrolyte, elevated temperatures
generation.mechanism: Increased active site density and improved charge transfer
generation.baseline: Pristine transition metal dichalcogenides without doping or defect engineering
generation.boundary: Limited by the stability of the material in the electrolyte and operating conditions
generation.uncertainty: The extent to which doping or defect engineering can enhance catalytic activity and durability is uncertain and requires further investigation

falsification_experiment.design: Electrochemical measurements of HER and HOR activity for pristine and doped/defect-engineered transition metal dichalcogenides
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the doped/defect-engineered material shows no significant improvement in catalytic activity or durability compared to the pristine material, the hypothesis is falsified
